subject: Post-call: performance & cost sprint — clarifying SLOs and next steps
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Bhandari <asha@medlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: performance & cost sprint — clarifying SLOs and next steps

Hi Asha — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed immediate next steps so we stay aligned: 

Key takeaways from today:
- Primary product: clinical-document summarization (batch + streaming UI).
- Target p95 latency for generative summaries: 350ms for short prompts (~256 tokens total).
- Concurrent active users: ~1200 peak, approximate request concurrency to backend ~250 during peaks (bursty).
- Throughput target: sustained ~600 reqs/min with spiky bursts up to 1200 reqs/min for short windows.
- Streaming requirement: yes — users expect progressive tokens within ~100-150ms of chunk emission.

What we need from you to size a realistic benchmark: 
1) Sample traffic (CSV) with timestamps and prompt length distribution — ideally last 7 days.
2) A representative prompt set (10–20 prompts) that covers short, medium, and long flows.
3) Clarify whether any requests include >1024 context tokens (helps pick model profile).

Proposed Redwood quick plan (48–72h prep):
- We run a targeted benchmark using your sample traffic and a split of model variants (Llama2-70B-q8*, Llama2-13B-q4f, and a float32 curated smaller model) to observe latency/throughput tradeoffs.
- Measure: p50/p95 latency, cold vs warm KV cache behavior, token cost per response, and streaming chunk latency.
- Suggested levers to explore during the benchmark: continuous batching (dynamic batch caps), prefix/KV caching for repeated clinical templates, and two quantization profiles (q4f aggressive vs q8_0 slower but higher quality).

Next steps I propose: 
- You share the traffic CSV (attachment OK) and 10 prompts by end of day tomorrow.
- We schedule a deep-dive benchmark kickoff with infra on Friday (30–45m).
- Marissa — can we queue a paid 2-week dedicated trial for MedLytics once Asha confirms the sample?

Happy to adjust — if any of the numbers above are off, correct me and we’ll re-target.

Thanks,
Michael Grant

Subject: Re: Post-call: performance & cost sprint — clarifying SLOs and next steps

Thanks Michael — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming the numbers look right from our side with a couple clarifications: 

- p95 target: 350ms for the short-summary flow (typical response size 80–150 tokens). For the long summary flow (500–700 token output) acceptable p95 is ~1.1s.
- Concurrency note: the 250 concurrent backend requests is correct, but those are not uniformly distributed — we see ~15% of sessions start a streaming flow that stays open for 3–7s.
- We have occasional >1024 context usage when clients attach history; approx 8% of calls.

Attached a sanitized sample of last 72h traffic (prod_traffic_sample_20260715.csv) and a 12-prompt representative set.

Two quick asks for your benchmark:
1) Can you include a streaming chunk-size experiment (emit every 64 vs 128 tokens) so we can evaluate perceived latency vs token cost?
2) Please estimate rough token-cost delta between q4f and q8 quantization profiles for the 80–150 token outputs.

We’re OK to move to the bench as soon as you confirm scope.

Regards,
Asha Bhandari
Head of Platform Engineering | MedLytics
asha@medlytics.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: performance & cost sprint — clarifying SLOs and next steps

Asha — thanks for the sample and the asks. Below is a pragmatic qualification checklist and the specific lever experiments we’ll run in the bench. I’ll include expected signals we’ll report back so you can evaluate tradeoffs.

Qualification checklist (what we’ll validate in the bench):
- p50/p95 latency for short (80–150 tok) and long (500–700 tok) outputs across model variants.
- End-to-end streaming latency (time to first token emitted, then time between chunks) at chunk sizes 64 and 128.
- Impact of KV/prefix caching on repeated template calls (measured as delta to token compute and p95 latency).
- Concurrency scaling: verify throughput at 250, 500, and 1000 concurrent request targets.
- Cold vs warm KV cache: quantify warmup period and effective cost reduction.
- Accuracy/quality check: small eval set for rouge/bertscore to ensure q4f stays acceptable for clinical summarization.

Lever experiments (we’ll vary one axis at a time):
1) Continuous batching: dynamic batch windows with max batch size caps tuned per model (we expect 8–12% cost improvement at your traffic profile while keeping p95 < target for short flows).
2) Prefix/KV caching: when templates repeat, we expect a 25–40% token compute reduction and ~20–30% p95 improvement for cached flows.
3) Quantization profiles: q4f (aggressive) vs q8 (balanced). q4f: ~30–45% inference cost reduction vs q8_0 but may show minor quality drift on longest outputs — we’ll attach sample diffs.
4) Model variants & fallbacks: default to 13B q4f for standard flows, fallback to 70B-q8* for difficult/long-context requests or high-importance sessions. Fallback policy reduces average cost but preserves quality on outliers.
5) Streaming tuning: smaller chunk sizes reduce time-to-first-token but increase per-token overhead. We’ll measure perceived latency (time-to-first + 95th inter-chunk gap) vs incremental cost.

Expected deliverables after bench (24–48h after run):
- Per-variant latency / throughput / cost matrix (CSV + dashboard link).
- Recommended production configuration: model default, quantization profile, batch window settings, and caching policy.
- Estimated monthly token cost delta for your current traffic at 3 candidate configs (conservative / balanced / aggressive cost optimization).

I attached a first-pass perf estimate workbook (redwood_perf_estimate_v1.xlsx) — it contains simple cost math and the assumptions we’ll verify. If that looks reasonable I’ll queue infra for the run.

Michael
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai
